qualification: Published v0.4.8 -> v0.4.9 Docker evaluation upgrade with both releases' published bundles, images and launchers, on one Linux arm64 Docker engine. The v0.4.8 installation was fresh, so it was on the portable lineage (0011-0018 -> 0019). Logical backup on the same host. Not the published lineage of a v0.4.8 upgraded from earlier releases, not off-host recovery, not Kubernetes.

host.load: Work outside the drill shared the host: concurrent Rust builds and a local Kubernetes cluster with restarting pods. From 07:50 to 08:21 UTC the macOS one-minute load average, sampled every 30 s, ranged from 6 to 85 on 18 cores; at 07:49 it was 79 with a fifteen-minute average of 37. No sample exists before 07:49. The OrbStack VM reported a load of 4 to 8. Timings here are an upper bound for this dataset, not a capacity measurement.

digest_method: snapshot.py: one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction as the bundled superuser synveda_owner over the local socket, so row-level security hides nothing; per public table, row count and SHA-256 over the sorted row_to_json text of its columns, with the column set frozen from the snapshot before the upgrade; ledger digest over version:checksum; audit prefix digest over seq, prev_hash, hash, occurred_at, actor, action, resource, outcome, payload and trace_id up to a bound; and every public constraint's pg_get_constraintdef, because 0019 changes only CHECK constraints and so moves no table digest

upgrade_with_injections.launcher_direction: after each refusal in migrating the launcher printed 'upgrade stopped after the schema change began. The installed release refuses this database: fix the cause and rerun this command to resume, or restore backup before-0-4-9'. After the lock refusal, 0019 had rolled back whole and v0.4.8's read-only check accepted the database; a v0.4.8 restart from that state was not tried. The direction to roll forward stayed correct.

realm_convergence_failure.observed: after migrated, Keycloak became healthy and the realm convergence child printed 'open projection was refused': its final check after enabling the realm, which reads the realm, user profile, client, mappers and admin group and reruns the scoped administrator login probe, quietly. Which step failed is not known. The steps before it printed no refusal
realm_convergence_failure.supervisor: synveda-realm-supervise records a failed generation and does not run convergence again for it; only a new Keycloak generation or a restarted container runs it again. Compose up --wait leaves the running unhealthy container in place, so rerunning the upgrade command waited on the same container
realm_convergence_failure.health_timing: the convergence health check allows a 900 s start period and 48 retries 5 s apart; the launcher waited 34 min 9 s. A failing streak of 54 at 07:49:09 places the end of the attempt near 07:44, which is a lead, not a measurement
realm_convergence_failure.cause: not established. The convergence script, its timeouts and the Keycloak version (26.7.2) are unchanged from v0.4.8; the Keycloak image digest differs. The projection helper JVM ran in about 300 ms at host load 83, which does not support a startup timeout. A CI run on AMD64 has seen realm convergence become unhealthy before (docs/CI.md)
realm_convergence_failure.recurrence: the clean second upgrade's realm convergence passed

why: the gateway's authority proof covers roles, ACLs, routines, triggers and forced row-level security, and its epoch stage reads the marker; 0019 changes only CHECK constraints, so with the marker at 0018 nothing it checks differs from v0.4.8's own head. The migrator and the check read the SQLx ledger and refused
